Verified the numbers quickly against the plan. Breakdown:
- Test window: 6 hours; target steady-state ~5k reqs/min (not 5k rps) — so approx 300k requests over the window.
- Average token/session in their sheet: ~33 tokens per request => ~10M tokens total (matches their estimate).
- Worst-case with retries and some long-context sessions: up to ~13M tokens.

Mitigations we recommend if we approve a top-up:
1) Provisional cap at 75k credit units (consumable only during 03/22 00:00-06:00 UTC) with automatic throttling once reached.
2) Enable prefix caching and batch size limits on their routes to reduce per-token cost during the soak. Ops can push recommended model config (we can apply as a managed setting for the test).
3) Require customer to accept a short promo amendment (DocuSign) that ties credits to the specific test window.

From a risk perspective, 75k is a reasonable middle ground — it covers the core run with some buffer if they apply batching. If they insist on full headroom (120k), we'd need finance approval for the additional incremental credit.

If Jonas/finance OKs 75k, I can set the promo and bake in throttles and observability hooks so CS can monitor consumption live.

-Karthik
